reviewed_by: Blind MATATAG curriculum reviewer (Grade 1-2 Data & Probability), scoring rendered samples against node competency text on 2026-08-14

samples_reviewed.question_text: Make a picture graph to show: apples: 30, bananas: 20, mangoes: 10, grapes: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Make a picture graph to show: Monday: 6, Tuesday: 16, Wednesday: 12, Thursday: 4. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for cats, dogs, birds and fish in the table. Each symbol stands for 5 items.
The pictograph shows roses, sunflowers, tulips and daisies. Fill in the table with the correct counts. Each symbol stands for 5 items.
Make a picture graph to show: roses: 2, sunflowers: 8, tulips: 18, daisies: 6. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 3, Grade 4, Grade 5 and Grade 6 in the table. Each symbol stands for 5 items.
Look at the pictograph. Write the correct count for each row in the table: basketball, volleyball, swimming, running, soccer and tennis. Each symbol stands for 10 items.
The pictograph shows red, blue, green, yellow, purple and orange. Fill in the table with the correct counts. Each symbol stands for 10 items.
The pictograph shows basketball, volleyball, swimming and running. Fill in the table with the correct counts.
Make a picture graph to show: apples: 10, bananas: 20, mangoes: 30, grapes: 20. Each 🍎 equals 10.
Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for red, blue, green and yellow in the table. Each symbol stands for 2 items.
Make a picture graph to show: basketball: 10, volleyball: 5, swimming: 15, running: 15. Each 🍎 equals 5.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Most items do what the competency states, but two things undercut it. First, the data-to-pictograph direction never makes the student use the scale: seed 42 asks "Make a picture graph to show: apples: 30, bananas: 20, mangoes: 10, grapes: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10." and the recorded correct answer is 30, 20, 10, 10 - the same four numbers already printed in the stem. Seed 43, "Make a picture graph to show: Monday: 6, Tuesday: 16, Wednesday: 12, Thursday: 4. Each 🍎 equals 2.", likewise answers 6, 16, 12, 4. Presenting data in a scaled pictograph requires dividing each value by the scale to get a row length, so as scored these items are a copy of the given values and the stated scale is inert. Second, the symbol in every build-a-graph item is an apple regardless of subject, so "Make a picture graph to show: basketball: 10, volleyball: 5, swimming: 15, running: 15. Each 🍎 equals 5." uses fruit to stand for sports. The reverse direction is sound: "Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for cats, dogs, birds and fish in the table. Each symbol stands for 5 items." answers 5, 10, 5, 10, which are genuine multiples of the stated scale.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names two directions and both are present in quantity. Data given in tabular form and turned into a scaled picture graph appears in seed 46, "Make a picture graph to show: roses: 2, sunflowers: 8, tulips: 18, daisies: 6. Each 🍎 equals 2.", and in seed 601, "Make a picture graph to show: apples: 10, bananas: 20, mangoes: 30, grapes: 20. Each 🍎 equals 10." The vice-versa direction, reading a scaled pictograph back into a table, appears in seed 45, "The pictograph shows roses, sunflowers, tulips and daisies. Fill in the table with the correct counts. Each symbol stands for 5 items.", and in seed 501, "Look at the pictograph. Write the correct count for each row in the table: basketball, volleyball, swimming, running, soccer and tennis. Each symbol stands for 10 items." All three standard Grade 2 scales are exercised - 2 in "Each symbol stands for 2 items.", 5 in "Each symbol stands for 5 items.", and 10 in "Each symbol stands for 10 items." - and both four-category and six-category data sets occur.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading and reasoning demand suits Grade 2 Quarter 3. Stems stay to one or two short sentences with the key stated separately, as in "Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for red, blue, green and yellow in the table. Each symbol stands for 2 items." The arithmetic implied by the pictograph-to-table items is repeated skip counting by 2, 5, or 10, which is on-grade: seed 500, "Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 3, Grade 4, Grade 5 and Grade 6 in the table. Each symbol stands for 5 items.", yields 25, 35, 20, 10, 30, 10 - all reachable by counting by fives. Six-row items add transcription volume rather than conceptual load. Category labels such as "red, blue, green, yellow, purple and orange" are everyday words, and no item requires multiplication notation, division notation, or half symbols.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Twelve samples cover two task types and several phrasings within each. The construction type appears with varied scales and contexts, e.g. "Make a picture graph to show: basketball: 10, volleyball: 5, swimming: 15, running: 15. Each 🍎 equals 5." versus "Make a picture graph to show: apples: 30, bananas: 20, mangoes: 10, grapes: 10. Each 🍎 equals 10." The reading type appears in three separate frames: "Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for cats, dogs, birds and fish in the table. Each symbol stands for 5 items.", "The pictograph shows red, blue, green, yellow, purple and orange. Fill in the table with the correct counts. Each symbol stands for 10 items.", and "Look at the pictograph. Write the correct count for each row in the table: basketball, volleyball, swimming, running, soccer and tennis. Each symbol stands for 10 items." Contexts span fruit, weekdays, animals, flowers, colours, sports, and grade levels, and row counts alternate between four and six.

competency_alignment.rationale: Eleven of twelve items keep difficulty inside this competency, varying it by scale size, category count, and direction of transfer while always involving a scaled pictograph. Seed 600 breaks that: "The pictograph shows basketball, volleyball, swimming and running. Fill in the table with the correct counts." states no symbol value at all, and its answers 16, 6, 5, 14 share no common factor, so the graph cannot be read as scaled - it is a one-picture-one-item pictograph. That is the earlier unscaled-pictograph skill, not this competency, whose object is expressly a pictograph with a scale as the other items make explicit with "Each symbol stands for 5 items." A student meeting seed 600 practises no scale reasoning. The drift is isolated rather than systemic, since every other reading item carries a key, e.g. "Each symbol stands for 10 items.", and every other construction item carries one, e.g. "Each 🍎 equals 2."

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Scales and totals are well chosen for Grade 2. The only scales used are 2, 5, and 10 - "Each symbol stands for 2 items.", "Each symbol stands for 5 items.", "Each symbol stands for 10 items.", and their construction-side equivalents "Each 🍎 equals 10." and "Each 🍎 equals 5." - which match the skip-counting sequences Grade 2 pupils already own. Data values are exact multiples of their stated scale, so no half symbol is ever needed: seed 602, "Count the pictures in each row of the pictograph, then write the counts for red, blue, green and yellow in the table. Each symbol stands for 2 items.", gives 12, 18, 10, 16, all even. Totals stay modest, peaking at 40 in "The pictograph shows red, blue, green, yellow, purple and orange. Fill in the table with the correct counts. Each symbol stands for 10 items.", and the implied row lengths stay short enough to draw, at most nine symbols in the scale-2 item.
